author.zh: 塞缪尔·巴特勒（署名“塞拉留斯”）

edition.en: Letter to the editor of The Press, Christchurch, New Zealand, signed Cellarius, as given on English Wikisource from Henry Festing Jones’s 1917 printing in The Note-Books of Samuel Butler, checked against A First Year in Canterbury Settlement with Other Early Essays (1914); the editor’s bracketed dateline is omitted, and so are the author’s footnotes printed in the 1914 edition.
edition.zh: 据英文维基文库所录（出自亨利·费斯廷·琼斯 1917 年版《塞缪尔·巴特勒笔记》）致新西兰基督城《新闻报》编辑的信，署名塞拉留斯，并与 1914 年版《坎特伯雷殖民地第一年及其他早期文章》核对；编者所加方括号内的日期行，以及 1914 年版所印的作者脚注，均从略。

basis.en: Published in 1863; Samuel Butler died in 1902, and the editor of the 1917 printing, Henry Festing Jones, in 1928.
basis.zh: 1863 年发表；作者卒于 1902 年，1917 年版编者亨利·费斯廷·琼斯卒于 1928 年。

note.en: Samuel Butler, then a young sheep farmer in New Zealand, sent this letter to the Christchurch Press under the name Cellarius four years after Darwin’s Origin of Species; it later grew into ‘The Book of the Machines’ in Erewhon. It treats machines as a new kingdom of life that evolves faster than plants or animals, with humans as its tenders. The closing call to destroy every machine is satire rather than a programme, and the letter is better read for its sharper point: that we are ‘ourselves creating our own successors’ and ought to think about what kind.
note.zh: 塞缪尔·巴特勒当时还是新西兰的一名年轻牧场主，在达尔文《物种起源》出版四年后，以“塞拉留斯”之名把这封信寄给基督城的《新闻报》；它后来扩展成《埃瑞璜》中的“机器之书”。信中把机器当作一个新的生命王国，进化得比植物和动物快得多，而人类是照料它们的人。结尾号召毁掉一切机器是讽刺，不是纲领；这封信更值得读的是它更尖锐的那一点：我们正在“亲自创造自己的继承者”，应当想想会是什么样的继承者。

excerpt.orig: It appears to us that we are ourselves creating our own successors
excerpt.en: It appears to us that we are ourselves creating our own successors
excerpt.zh: 在我们看来，正是我们自己在创造自己的继承者。
